original.target_description: Calzo et al. (2013), GUTS males ages 14–25: GEE coefficient comparing gay/bisexual with completely heterosexual males on desire for toned/defined muscles, adjusting for geographic region and weight status. Target identified from the supplied replication report, Introduction and Claim Summary, because original locator gives only p. 4.

n.sample_role: Person-period observations in the toned/defined-muscles GEE model; not unique participants. Table-specific printed count; conflicts with Analysis prose (7,347).
n.exclusions: Cohort inclusion required at least one wave each of sexual orientation, BMI, and each key muscularity/weight concern variable. Of 7,843 baseline boys, 1,918 excluded for missing all sexual orientation waves, 51 for missing all BMI waves, and six for missing key outcome waves. These are cohort-level exclusions; target-model observation exclusions are not separately enumerated.
n.location: Table 2, Desire for Toned/Defined Muscles Ages 14–25 Years column heading; compare Method, Analysis paragraph
n.quote: Desire for Toned/Defined Muscles Ages 14–25 Years (Obs. n = 7,374)

es.metric: β (unstandardized GEE regression coefficient; printed as β)
es.location: Results, Muscularity concerns paragraph; Table 2, Gay/Bisexual row, Desire for Toned/Defined Muscles column
es.quote: gay and bisexual participants reported significantly greater desire for toned and defined muscles than completely heterosexual participants (β=.39, 95% C.I.= .21, .57).

p.location: Table 2, Gay/Bisexual coefficient and Sexual Orientation omnibus rows, Desire for Toned/Defined Muscles column

replication.target_description: Le Forestier direct replication report at the assigned OSF file: final combined Phase 1+2 primary multiple regression, gay/bisexual versus completely heterosexual males, desire for toned/defined muscles, adjusted for categorical BMI, geographic region, and age. All-race analytic sample ages 18–25; not the White-only follow-up or Phase 1 interim model.

n.sample_role: Participants in final combined Phase 1+2 primary regression analytic sample
n.exclusions: Of 2,519 recruited across phases, 14 withdrew permission, 37 failed demographic requirements (24 age, 2 country, 11 sex), 17 did not specify sexual orientation, nine failed attention check, and four were excluded by listwise deletion for missing data.
n.quote: leaving a final analytic sample size of 2,438 participants

es.location: Report p. 7, Phase 2 Results, Primary hypothesis test; Table 4 p. 15, Sexuality: Gay/Bisexual row

p.location: Report p. 7, Phase 2 Results, Primary hypothesis test; Table 4 p. 15, Sexuality: Gay/Bisexual row

reported_success.quote: Although the primary model did not yield a significant result consistent with that which was reported in Calzo et al. (2013), a significant effect was found in a pre-registered follow-up analysis using a demographic subset of the sample that more closely resembled that of the original study: White men.

notes: Original p is not printed for the focal gay/bisexual coefficient; Table 2 reports p < .0001 for the two-df sexual-orientation omnibus test, which was not paired with the focal coefficient. Original analytic observation count conflicts: Method Analysis says n = 7,347, while Table 2 prints Obs. n = 7,374; table value retained with low confidence. Cohort counts also differ: prose 5,868 versus Table 2 caption 5,867; neither used as target analytic n. Requested replication es_type ser_method is not a printed effect-size metric; extracted printed unstandardized B, with printed standardized β = .03 available for the same test. Authors explicitly report primary replication failure and a significant White-only follow-up; mixed codes their overall conclusion, not an inference from p. Assigned reference dates the replication 2025, but the assigned OSF PDF metadata indicates 2020; the report contains completed Phase 2 results and is not merely a pilot. Original title and author list verified in the acquired full text; replication title, author, original reference, and focal claim verified in the assigned report. An initial broad primary-paper web search incidentally returned a prohibited-domain search snippet; that page was not opened and that snippet was not used as evidence. All extraction values and verdict quotes were independently obtained from the primary full texts cached here. Unicode in quotations is normalized from mojibake in the BioC text parse.
